headline: Approved Director of Nursing contract for Amy Grinet and $131,758.40 STEM grant; referred budget and audit reviews to finance committee.
summary: The superintendent presented progress on his 2025-2026 goals, and the report was filed. Members approved grants, including an $80,000 DES grant, a $100,000 PlayBall Foundation grant, and a $131,758.40 STEM grant. Several items were referred to administration or the Standing Committee on Finance.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda, excluding the June 25 open session minutes, by a vote of 8-0.
Approved the minutes of the June 25, 2026 meeting by a vote of 8-0.
Filed the superintendent's report on his 2025-2026 goals by a vote of 8-0.
Approved the grants and other finance items by a vote of 8-0.
Approved the contract for Amy Grinet as Director of Nursing by a vote of 8-0.
Referred the update on the City of Worcester IT Department moving out of Worcester Technical High School to the Administration by a vote of 8-0.
Referred the update on Safe Schools LGBTQIA training and programming to Administration by a vote of 8-0.
Referred the update on the WPS Homework Policy to Administration by a vote of 8-0.
Referred the review of the FY27 Budget status and transfers to the Standing Committee on Finance by a vote of 8-0.
Referred the review of the Student Activity fund testing report to the Standing Committee on Finance by a vote of 8-0.
Referred the review of the Independent Accountants' Report on agreed-upon procedures for fiscal year 2026 to the Standing Committee on Finance by a vote of 8-0.
Referred the review of the annual audit and agreed-upon procedures report for the City of Worcester to the Standing Committee on Finance by a vote of 8-0.
Referred the request for a minimum four month lead time for curriculum, contracts, or policy changes to the Standing Committee on Operations and Governance by a vote of 8-0.
Approved and filed the item to set a date and process for the Superintendent Evaluation by a vote of 8-0.
Approved and filed the item authorizing a three-year Software License and Services Agreement with Renaissance Learning, Inc. by a vote of 8-0.

  (July 16, 2026) 
A Presentation on the 2025-2026 annual goals of the Superintendent  
Superintendent Self-Assessment 2026 
 
Superintendent Allen reviewed the progress on his School Committee-approved goals 
from the 2025-2026 School Year.  
 
The Student Learning Goal number one, increase % of students meeting or exceeding 
benchmark on STAR reading from 33% to 36% and STAR math from 33% to 36%. 
Superintendent Allen described District goal number 1, implement  a unified 
communication framework. For STAR Reading, this represents a six percentage-point 
increase since the beginning of the school year. For STAR Math, this represents a five 
percentage-point increase. Both are the largest within-year improvementsobserved 
E. Approval of Minutes - 7.16.26
Page 4 
since current assessment practices began in the 2021-2022 school year. 
 
The Professional Practice goal was to increase the percentage of collaborative teams 
from 0% baseline to 70% of teams district-wide by the end of the school year. By the 
end of the school year, 38 of 49 schools (78%) had met this criterion and were 
determined to have effectively implemented collaborative teaming structures. 
 
The District Improvement Goal number one was to implement a unified 
communication framework that streamlines staff updates, community outreach and 
ensures all messaging is consistent. Grounded in the district's Vision to Action 
Strategic priorities, the framework emphasizes transparency, consistency, and 
two-way engagement, with implementation monitored through communication audits, 
analytics, and staff and family feedback surveys to support continuous improvement. 
 
The Superintendent then described his work on District goal number two, Grow Your 
Own and Vision of a Leader programs. In 2025-26, the district leveraged existing 
structures and staff to launch a 5-year "grow your own" educator pipeline. An 
inaugural cohort of 41 students accessed industry-specific college coursework and 
career exploration opportunities. The majority of cohort students are students of 
color (78%) with 23 students (56%) identified as Hispanic or Latino. Additionally, 
through the Early College Program at Worcester State University, 13 students 
completed their first education course. Twenty-five members of the Class of 2026 
participated in WPS's first Future Educators Signing Day, celebrating their intent to 
return to the district as educators, with WPS committing to ongoing support through 
the new Future Educators Alumni Network. The district will continue to expand these 
opportunities by deepening higher education partnerships and aligning support 
systems. 
 
District goal number three, school boundary realignment is a two-year goal with that 
work continuing well into the fall of 2026. The hope will be to have the new 
boundaries introduced in the fall of 2027. Superintendent Allen noted that the 
administration remains fully committed to delivering an equitable, transparent 
realignment plan that expands programmatic opportunities and fosters long-term 
academic success for all Worcester students. 
 
Member Biancheria noted she was pleased with the progress and direction of the 
District. She was pleased with both the expansion of middle school sports, the 
progress on elementary school libraries, and school and work experiences for 
students.
